proof:
The adjacent midpoint inclusions are $(D+R)/2\subseteq T$ and $(T+E_L)/2\subseteq R$. For the first, coordinates are at least $-1$ and their sum is at most $((-2+3\sigma)+2b)/2=-5\sigma/2$. For the second the coordinate range is contained in $[(-1+r-L)/2,(2+r)/2]\subseteq[-1,b]$. In each continuous direction these inclusions give concavity of the piecewise-affine interpolation of the four support values. Any convex combination of the prescribed fibers landing at an integer base then satisfies the support inequality of its prescribed fiber, by concavity. This proves canonicality and the exact base set. The positive definite matrix $\Sigma$ is continuous in $L$ and invariant under coordinate exchange because every fiber has that symmetry. The width is positive for every nonzero $u$ when $h>0$.

At a mark with barycentrics $(1-2t,t,t)$ near $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, suppose a cap isolates vertex $i$ and meets its two incident edges at fractions $\ell_j,\ell_k$ of their lengths, measured from $i$. The plane through the mark gives $y_j/\ell_j+y_k/\ell_k=1$. The area is $V\ell_j\ell_k$, uniquely minimized at $\ell_j=2y_j,\ell_k=2y_k$ by AM–GM. This minimum is nondegenerate in the angle: writing $m=y_j/\ell_j$, the area is $Vy_jy_k/[m(1-m)]$, with a strict positive second derivative at $m=1/2$, and $m$ is a local regular coordinate for the line angle through the mark. Indeed the intercept on an incident edge varies with nonzero derivative under rotation while that edge is transverse and does not pass through the mark. At the centroid a cap containing two vertices has area at least $V/2$. In the complement, if it cuts out the third vertex alone, the two intersection fractions $a,b$ from that vertex obey $1/a+1/b=3$ and $0<a,b\le1$. The product $ab$ is at most $1/2$ since for $p=1/a,q=1/b$ one has $p+q=3$, $p,q\ge1$, and $pq\ge2$. If all vertices are captured the bound is immediate. Thus by compactness near the centroid no other direction minimizes its branch, and the three minimizing directions are interior to their angular branches. The area formulas follow. Equalizing $q_A+v=q_B=q_C$ gives $12t^2-4t+\sigma^2=0$ with the stated root near $1/3$. Since $1/4<t\le1/3$, $4Vt(1-2t)\ge2$, while $4Vt^2+v\le2+v$.

Write a cap through the diagonal mark with continuous coordinate $Y=(s,s)$ as $a z+u\cdot(X-Y)\ge0$. The smoothed integrand is one for nonnegative margin, zero when the margin is at or below the negative width, and linear in between. If $A$ maximizes, then $u_x,u_y\le0$. Failure to capture all $D$ supplies $X_D\in D$ with $a>u\cdot(X_D-Y)$. On the whole square $[-1/2,1/2]^2\subset R$ the margin at base $1$ then exceeds $u\cdot(X_D+X-2Y)>0$, since the two coordinates of $X_D+X-2Y$ are negative and $u\ne0$. This captures area at least one, greater than $v$. Thus outside mass in this branch is at least $v$, with equality requiring full $D$ and zero $R,E_L$. Other branches have nonnegative outside mass.

These minimum outside patterns are attained with strict margins at the zero-width own minima. For $A$ use $u_A=(-1,-1),a_A=-3$, giving positive margin on $D$ and negative margins on $R,E_L$. For $B$ use $u_B=(1,\delta)$, $\delta=3-1/t=O(\sigma^2)<0$, obtained by equating the proper intercepts on $BA,BC$. Use $a_B=-1+(7/2)\sigma$. Maximizing the margin on $D$ gives $-a_B-1+3\sigma-\delta-s(1+\delta)=-\sigma/2+O(\sigma^2)$, and on $R$ gives $a_B+b-\delta-s(1+\delta)=-\sigma/2+O(\sigma^2)$. On $E_L$ it gives $a_B+r+\delta(r-L)-s(1+\delta)<-1$ for small $\sigma$ uniformly in the displayed $L$ range. Coordinate exchange gives the $C$ witness.

Fix such a $\sigma$. The ordinary proper cap area is smooth near each minimizing direction and threshold, since both edge intercepts are smooth there. Averaging it over outward displacements in $[0,h\sqrt{u^\top\Sigma u}]$ remains smooth at $h=0$ (use the integral over a fixed unit interval). The nondegenerate angular critical points persist by the implicit function theorem and the strict gap away from them excludes other minima by compactness. All estimates are uniform for $L$ in its compact range. At the diagonal $q_B=q_C$. At $h=0$ the derivative of $q_A+v-q_B$ in $s$ is $V(24t-4)/3>0$, so the implicit function theorem gives the nearby diagonal $s(h,L)$ and the exact equalization. The strict outside margins persist throughout the smoothing strips for the three selected tilts. The corresponding three normals remain spanning and positively balanced, because $(-1,-1),(1,\delta),(\delta,1)$ have that property at zero width.

Every nonzero continuous normal belongs to a maximum-vertex branch. Its own mass is at least that branch minimum, and the outside lower bounds already established give total mass at least $Q_T$. Equality forces one of the unique continuous directions and the listed saturated outside pattern. Pure-base caps through base zero include all of $T$, so have strictly larger mass. At positive width the derivative for an outside fiber is the volume in its open transition strip divided by the width, since each strip boundary is a planar null set. Saturated full or zero capture has zero strip volume. Finally, for any other mark on fiber zero, its displacement from $Y_T$ has positive projection on at least one of the three spanning positively balanced normals. Keeping that witness tilt and direction and passing through the new mark raises the threshold, strictly losing mass initially on its proper own strip, with monotonicity for all larger increases. This proves uniqueness of the maximum.

statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\{A=(-1,-1),B=(2,-1),C=(-1,2)\}$, $V=|T|=9/2$, $D=(1-\sigma)A+\sigma T$, $v=V\sigma^2$, $b=1-4\sigma$, $r=-8\sigma$, $R=[-1,b]^2$ and $E_L=[r-L,r]^2$. For sufficiently small fixed $\sigma>0$ with $\sigma\le10^{-4}$ and $2\sqrt\sigma\le L\le4\sqrt\sigma$, these are the exact positive fibers at $-1,0,1,2$ of their canonical hull. Let $\Sigma$ be the pooled within-fiber covariance, weighted by the actual fiber volumes, and use outward uniform smoothing of width $h\sqrt{u^\top\Sigma u}$ for a continuous normal $u$. A cap's mass is the average of the ordinary closed cap masses with the threshold shifted outward by a uniform amount in that width. Raw depth is the minimum mass over ambient oriented cap normals through the given mark.

For every sufficiently small $h>0$, uniformly in $L$, the unique maximizing mark in fiber $0$ is $Y_T=(0,s(h,L),s(h,L))$. If $q_i$ is the own smoothed cap mass minimized over continuous normals maximizing on vertex $i\in\{A,B,C\}$, then its depth is $Q_T=q_A+v=q_B=q_C$. Each branch has a unique minimizing continuous direction. Every active cap in branch $A$ fully captures $D$ and misses $R,E_L$. Every active cap in branch $B$ or $C$ misses all three outside fibers. Thus every active cap has zero outside transition coarea, the outside contribution to the derivative of mass with respect to outward threshold displacement. At zero width $s=3t-1$ with $t=(1+\sqrt{1-3\sigma^2})/6$, $q_A=4Vt^2$, $q_B=q_C=4Vt(1-2t)$ and $2\le Q_T(0,L)\le2+v$.
title: All active caps at an actual smoothed triangle source have three prescribed capture patterns
